dossier.purpose: LanceDB is an embedded (in-process) multimodal/vector database library built on the Lance columnar format. It has a Rust core (rust/lancedb), Python (PyO3) and Node.js/TypeScript (napi-rs) SDKs, and a Java client limited to LanceDB Cloud/Enterprise. Tables live on local disk, memory:// or object storage. It offers ANN vector indexes (IVF-Flat/PQ/SQ/RQ, IVF-HNSW variants), BM25 full-text and substring indexes, scalar indexes, hybrid search with rerankers, table versions/tags/branches, and an optional embedding-function registry that calls external or local embedding models. It is a storage/search library: this repository contains no repository crawler, code-aware chunker, CLI, MCP server or daemon (searches and manifests below).

claims.claim: "The Multimodal AI Lakehouse"; "LanceDB is designed for fast, scalable, and production-ready vector search. It is built on top of the Lance columnar format."
"Fast Vector Search: Search billions of vectors in milliseconds with state-of-the-art indexing."
"Comprehensive Search: Support for vector similarity search, full-text search and SQL."
"Multimodal Support: Store, query and filter vectors, metadata and multimodal data (text, images, videos, point clouds, and more)."
"Advanced Features: Zero-copy, automatic versioning, manage versions of your data without needing extra infrastructure. GPU support in building vector index."
"Open Source & Local: 100% open source, runs locally or in your cloud. No vendor lock-in."
"Cloud and Enterprise: Production-scale vector search with no servers to manage. Complete data sovereignty and security."
"Seamless Integration: Python, Node.js, Rust, and REST APIs for easy integration. Native Python and Javascript/Typescript support."
"Rich Ecosystem: Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Apache-Arrow, Pandas, Polars, DuckDB and more on the way."
Install is deferred to external docs: "Follow the Quickstart doc to set up LanceDB locally." (the README itself contains no install command)
SDK table lists Python, Typescript and Rust SDKs plus a REST API (docs.lancedb.com/api-reference/rest); Java is not mentioned in the README
(Absence) The README makes no statement about an MCP server, a CLI, Claude Code/Codex integration, code or repository indexing, embedding services, or telemetry; the whole file was read

platforms.wsl2: unknown - no mention of WSL or WSL2 anywhere in the repository (case-insensitive search of all non-lock files). A WSL2 distro would be an ordinary Linux target for the wheels/npm packages, but this is neither documented nor tested upstream.

platforms.gpu: yes (limited) - the only GPU feature is IVF vector-index building in the Python SDK via `accelerator=` (e.g. 'cuda'), which dispatches to the optional `pylance` package (python/python/lancedb/table.py:3141-3186; python/python/lancedb/index.py:340-342). It is rejected on LanceDB Cloud (python/python/lancedb/remote/table.py:500-502), has 'Only in Python SDK' status in the Rust docs (rust/lancedb/src/lib.rs:13-16) and no Node option. Embedding models pick their own device (e.g. SentenceTransformerEmbeddings.device defaults to 'cpu', python/python/lancedb/embeddings/sentence_transformers.py:26-27). Nothing requires a GPU.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home code found in the Rust, Python, Node or Java sources: searches for posthog/sentry/telemetry/analytics/usage-tracking return only the opt-in OpenTelemetry metrics bridge, which installs a process-global recorder only when instrument_lancedb_metrics() is called and reports into the application's own MeterProvider (python/python/lancedb/otel.py:35-100; nodejs/lancedb/otel.ts:20-50; rust/lancedb/Cargo.toml:165-173). Local mode (`lancedb.connect('<path>')` or `memory://`) needs no account and contacts no LanceDB server (python/python/lancedb/__init__.py:187-217, 289-301). A `db://` URI switches to LanceDB Cloud/Enterprise, requires an API key (arg or LANCEDB_API_KEY) (__init__.py:269-288), talks to https://<db>.<region>.api.lancedb.com unless host_override is set (rust/lancedb/src/remote/client.rs:531-538), and sends x-api-key (client.rs:631-638), a `LanceDB-Rust-Client/<ver>` user agent (client.rs:161) and, only if configured via ClientConfig.user_id or LANCEDB_USER_ID, an `x-lancedb-user-id` header 'for tracking purposes' (client.rs:100-106,181-200). OAuth flows contact the configured issuer or Azure IMDS 169.254.169.254 (rust/lancedb/src/remote/oauth.rs:20-21). Network is also used when a provider is selected: OpenAI (default https://api.openai.com/v1; rust/lancedb/src/embeddings/openai.rs:129-133; python/python/lancedb/embeddings/openai.py:124-140), Ollama (default http://localhost:11434; python/python/lancedb/embeddings/ollama.py:27), Cohere/Gemini/Bedrock/Voyage/Jina/Watsonx etc. (python/python/lancedb/embeddings/__init__.py:6-23), and Hugging Face hub model downloads for local models (rust/lancedb/src/embeddings/sentence_transformers.rs:142-164; nodejs/lancedb/embedding/transformers.ts:77-95; python/python/lancedb/embeddings/sentence_transformers.py:83-88). s3://, gs://, az:// URIs use the cloud SDKs (python/python/lancedb/__init__.py:192-213). Docs website only (not the library): docs/mkdocs.yml:144-150 enables Google Analytics (G-B7NFM40W74) and docs/src/extra_js/reo.js:1 loads https://static.reo.dev/<id>/reo.js. Dev/CI builds read pre-release Lance wheels from https://pypi.fury.io/lance-format/ and /lancedb/ (python/Makefile:1; .github/workflows/python.yml:31).

code.architecture: Cargo workspace with three members, rust/lancedb, nodejs and python (Cargo.toml:1-3), on exact-pinned Lance crates (=12.0.0), Arrow 58 and DataFusion 54 (Cargo.toml:16-53). Core crate rust/lancedb/src: connection.rs and database/{listing,namespace}.rs (local FS, memory, object stores, Lance namespaces); table.rs plus table/* (create_index, add_data, merge, optimize, schema_evolution, query, dataset, checkpoint); query.rs and query/hybrid.rs; index.rs (+scalar/vector; Auto, BTree, Bitmap, LabelList, FM substring, BM25 FTS, IvfFlat/Pq/Sq/Rq, IvfHnswPq/Sq/Flat, index.rs:29-102); embeddings.rs (+openai, sentence_transformers via candle, bedrock) with an in-memory registry (:80-113); rerankers/rrf.rs; remote/* (REST client, OAuth, SQL; feature `remote`); dataloader/permutation; materialized_view; function.rs. Bindings: python/src/*.rs (PyO3) + python/python/lancedb (db.py, table.py, query.py, pydantic.py, embeddings/ with ~17 providers, rerankers/ ~10, remote/, otel.py); nodejs/src/*.rs (napi-rs) + nodejs/lancedb/*.ts (embedding/{openai,transformers}, rerankers/rrf); java/lancedb-core (REST namespace client only). It runs in-process with no server. Embedding configuration is optional: the function name and args are stored in Arrow schema metadata key `embedding_functions` (python embeddings/registry.py:147-158; nodejs embedding/registry.ts:146-166) and, on string queries, the query is embedded with it (python query.py:975-984; nodejs table.ts:1247-1269). Version history: version/checkout/checkout_tag/checkout_latest/restore/list_versions, tags and branches (rust table.rs:2036-2121,2341,2372; python table.py:2394-2444; nodejs table.ts:855-915). Not present in the repo: repository/file crawling, code-aware chunking (no tree-sitter/AST matches; python/python/lancedb/context.py:14-23 is a pandas row-window helper), file-change tracking, CLI, MCP server, daemon.
code.packaging_and_release: All four SDKs share one version (0.39.0) and one `vX.Y.Z` tag (release_process.md:3-7; .bumpversion.toml:1-2); a manual `Create release commit` workflow bumps and tags (.github/workflows/make-release-commit.yml:12-73); stable releases about every 2 weeks, preview (beta) releases in between and possibly deleted after 6 months (release_process.md:16-25). Tag `v*` triggers: gh-release.yml (GitHub Release with generated changelog only; no files, checksums or signatures attached, :74-85); pypi-publish.yml (maturin wheels: manylinux_2_28 x86_64 and aarch64, `lancedb-compat` x86-64-v2 variant, macOS arm64, Windows x64, :30-163; stable tags published with pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1 under `id-token: write` (:164-214), beta tags uploaded to Gemfury with a FURY_TOKEN secret (:182-204)); npm-publish.yml (7 napi targets, tests on mac arm64/linux x64/linux arm64 before publish, `npm config set provenance true`, beta -> `--tag preview`, :35-449; also runs nightly); cargo-publish.yml (crates.io via rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action, skips *-beta* tags, :3-39); java-publish.yml (Maven OSSRH with GPG signing, :36-65). No checksum, SBOM, cosign or SLSA steps were found in .github (searched); only npm provenance and Maven GPG signing exist as signed/attested outputs. Most third-party actions are pinned by tag rather than SHA (e.g. pypi-publish.yml:212).

Test files, approximate: Rust 67 src files with inline #[cfg(test)] modules + 6 integration files in rust/lancedb/tests/ (blob_integration, embedding_registry_test, embeddings_parallel_test, first_class_function_slice1/2, object_store_test) + src/remote/sql_test.rs; Python 56 in python/python/tests (45 top-level + 11 under docs/) + 2 in python/tests (test_oauth.py, test_otel.py, a path none of the CI pytest commands I read targets: run_tests/action.yml:27-31, python.yml:159,266) + ci/tests/test_set_lance_version.py; Node 20 `*.test.ts` in nodejs/__test__ + 9 in nodejs/examples; Java 2 classes. Roughly 165 test files in total. CI workflows (.github/workflows): rust.yml (fmt, clippy with/without `remote`, cargo-deny, no-lockfile build, Linux all-features tests with localstack docker-compose, remote tests needing a secret, macOS 14/15, Windows x64+arm64, MSRV 1.91.0); python.yml (ruff, pyright, doctest, Linux py3.10/3.13 with integration tests, macOS 14, Windows, min-deps); nodejs.yml (biome, clippy, Linux Node 22/24/26 jest + docs-drift check + example tests against ci/mock_openai.py, macOS 15); java.yml (checkstyle + `mvnw clean install`, Java 17); npm-publish.yml and pypi-publish.yml (cross-platform build dry runs; Windows Node tests disabled, npm-publish.yml:331-333); dev.yml (PR labeler, conventional-commit title check); ci-scripts.yml; license-header-check.yml; typos.yml; docs.yml; docs-link-check.yml (nightly); plus the release and Codex maintenance workflows. Embedding providers that need live services (OpenAI, Ollama, ...) are tested only in `slow`-marked, skip-if-unavailable tests that default CI excludes (python/python/tests/test_embeddings_slow.py:477-499; run_tests/action.yml:27-31), and python/lancedb/embeddings/*.py is excluded from doctests (python/pyproject.toml:116).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:45 'Support for vector similarity search, full-text search and SQL'
claim_checks.evidence: Vector search (python/python/lancedb/table.py:1614-1698; rust/lancedb/src/query.rs) and native BM25 FTS (rust/lancedb/src/index.rs:57-77; Tantivy FTS was removed, table.py:3529-3533) are implemented, as is a substring (FM) index (index.rs:52-55). SQL *queries* are remote-only: python/python/lancedb/db.py:799-803 says 'Local connections do not support SQL', rust/lancedb/src/database.rs:336-345 returns NotSupported by default, and docs/src/python/python.md:31-41 documents SQL only for a remote database. claim_checks.claim: README.md:47 'Zero-copy, automatic versioning, manage versions of your data without needing extra infrastructure'
claim_checks.evidence: Rust Table::version/checkout/checkout_tag/checkout_latest/restore/list_versions (rust/lancedb/src/table.rs:2036-2121), tags (:2341) and branches (:2372); Python table.py:2394-2444 ('Data is not copied' on restore, :2431-2432); Node table.ts:855-915. claim_checks.claim: python/python/lancedb/table.py:1683-1684 (docstring): for a string query, 'the query type is vector if the table has embedding functions else fts'
claim_checks.evidence: python/python/lancedb/query.py:975-984 embeds the string with the vector column's embedding function (compute_query_embeddings_with_retry) and runs vector search, else falls back to FTS. The embedding config is stored in the Arrow schema metadata key `embedding_functions` at create time (db.py:1944-1949; embeddings/registry.py:130-158) and re-read on open (table.py:3782-3795). risks: Scope: the repo is a storage/search library, not a code-search tool. Chunking, re-indexing and the agent-facing tool layer would have to be built on top.

Claude Code/Codex integration cannot be verified: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:10 and .agents/plugins/marketplace.json:11 reference ./plugins/lancedb, which does not exist at v0.39.0. The described purpose is writing LanceDB code (marketplace.json:11), and the only Codex assets are maintainer-only (.agents/skills/lancedb-update-lance-dependency/SKILL.md:1-12; .github/workflows/codex-fix-ci.yml).

Embedding-service compatibility is narrow in practice: the built-in OpenAI functions only know three OpenAI model names in Python (embeddings/openai.py:69-78; table.py:873,892), Node (nodejs/lancedb/embedding/openai.ts:60-71) and Rust (rust/lancedb/src/embeddings/openai.rs:38-51), and Node exposes no base-URL option (openai.ts:10-13,48-52). Python has a native Ollama function (embeddings/ollama.py:17-33). Live-service embedding tests are slow-marked and excluded from default CI (python/python/tests/test_embeddings_slow.py:477-499; .github/workflows/run_tests/action.yml:27-31).

Recoverable-state caveats: embedding functions must be re-registered each process and `$var:` secrets re-set ('Variables are reset in new Python sessions', embeddings/base.py:73-77; registry.py:160-174); the Rust registry is in-memory (rust/lancedb/src/embeddings.rs:91-113); read_consistency_interval defaults to None so concurrent writers are not seen until checkout_latest() (python/python/lancedb/__init__.py:140-149; rust/lancedb/src/connection.rs:867-870); optimize() prunes versions older than 7 days by default (table.py:2109-2111), so old versions are not retained indefinitely.

Platform: default x86_64 builds need AVX2/FMA/F16C and crash with 'Illegal instruction' on older CPUs (python/README.md:11-15; .cargo/config.toml:43-47); no Intel-macOS wheel or npm package although nodejs/README.md:14-16 claims it (pypi-publish.yml:100-103; nodejs/package.json:23-34); no musl Python wheels (pypi-publish.yml:30-61); WSL2 undocumented; Python >=3.10 and Node >=22 required (python/pyproject.toml:19; nodejs/package.json:69-71); Windows Node tests are disabled in release CI (npm-publish.yml:331-333).

Maintenance/stability: pre-1.0 (0.39.0) with the 'Development Status :: 3 - Alpha' classifier (python/pyproject.toml:28); breaking changes land in minor releases, and Lance minor bumps count as breaking (release_process.md:65-92); Lance crates are exact-pinned at =12.0.0 (Cargo.toml:16-29); releases about every 2 weeks and preview releases may be removed after 6 months (release_process.md:16-25).

Security hygiene: no SECURITY.md or disclosure policy; deny.toml:36-117 ignores 15 RUSTSEC advisories, including a tantivy segfault on malformed input (RUSTSEC-2025-0003, :54-59) and pyo3 advisories affecting the Python bindings (RUSTSEC-2026-0176/0177, :87-91). SentenceTransformerEmbeddings and the CrossEncoder reranker default trust_remote_code=True, which executes model-repo code fetched from Hugging Face (python/python/lancedb/embeddings/sentence_transformers.py:30,37,86-88; rerankers/cross_encoder.py:31,42).

Release/CI supply chain: GitHub Releases carry no assets, checksums or attestations (gh-release.yml:74-85); only npm provenance (npm-publish.yml:440) and Maven GPG signing (java-publish.yml:45-65) are signed; most third-party actions are tag-pinned (pypi-publish.yml:212); license-header-check.yml:26 pipes an install script from a mutable `master` URL into bash; maintainer workflows run `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` with write-scoped tokens (codex-fix-ci.yml:19-22,179); dev and CI builds pull pre-release Lance wheels from a third-party Gemfury index (python/Makefile:1; python.yml:31).

checks.statement: The OpenAIEmbeddings docstring says it works with open models behind an OpenAI-compatible API (an Ollama model name plus base_url). Verified 'no': _ndims accepts only three OpenAI model names, and ndims() is called whenever embeddings are auto-computed. Node and Rust are restricted the same way.
checks.note: base_url is a field (openai.py:46) and is passed to openai.OpenAI (:128-129). _ndims (:69-78) raises ValueError('Unknown model name …') for any other name, even when dim is set. table.py:892 calls conf.function.ndims() on every auto-embedded batch, and :873 calls it when building the vector field without a schema. In Node, OpenAIOptions has only apiKey and model (:10-13), the client config is only apiKey (:48-52), and ndims() throws for unknown models (:60-71). Rust FromStr accepts only the three models (:38-51) but offers api_base() (:129-133). OllamaEmbeddings is registered at ollama.py:17, and its ndims() embeds 'foo' through the server (:32-33).
